meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition with Germanic influences; unitary national legal system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) BIT network — 80+ active bilateral investment treaties
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — free movement of capital, establishment, and digital services

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on anti-money laundering; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Art. 100-1 et seq.); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities, the RBE registrar, and obliged entities conducting customer due diligence have full statutory access; general public access is restricted to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest, consistent with the CJEU ruling of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte notarié de constitution) incorporating the Articles of Association (Statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in the district of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial act — no apostille required; the notary authenticates the deed and files it ex officio with the RCS and RBE

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif) submitted to the RBE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RBE Department, filed through the incorporating notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Electronic filing with notarial certification; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each beneficial owner, manager, and statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry, passport authority, or notary in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Apostille Convention member states) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record extract (certificat de bonnes mœurs) for each manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police authority in the country of residence or nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and board resolution approving the Luxembourg investment — for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry and board of directors in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of source of funds for each founding shareholder (anti-fraud and AML verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing banking institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or apostille where demanded by the notary's AML policy; certified translation into French, German, or English

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: MANDATORY PROTOCOL: (1) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening of all UBOs, managers, directors, shareholders holding over 25%, and authorized signatories, applying FATF and EU AMLD definitions; (2) Consolidated sanctions screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Council Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance freezing measures; (3) adverse media and negative news checks; (4) jurisdictional risk rating under CSSF guidance; (5) enhanced due diligence where any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or complex ownership layer is identified; (6) ongoing transaction and onboarding monitoring after incorporation under CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal www.lbr.lu and eJustice filing system (justice.public.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in one of the administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German, or Luxembourgish) or in any other language using Latin script, with mandatory transliteration into Latin characters for non-Latin scripts. The name must be distinctive, lawful, non-misleading, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, a protected trademark, or a name reserved by another applicant.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires prior CAA authorization)
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement / Investment Fund (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Société de gestion / Management Company / ManCo (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Prestataire de services de paiement / Payment Services Provider (requires prior CSSF authorization)
État / State / Government / Commune / Ministère (misleading official character prohibited)
Luxembourg / Luxembourgeoise / Luxembourgish (requires prior ministerial authorization)
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce (requires statutory authorization)
Union Européenne / European Union / UE (prohibited where misleading)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 days by filing a renewal request through the LBR portal before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may: (i) submit a written administrative objection to the RCS registrar (LBR) within 15 days of the rejection notice; (ii) if the objection is denied, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (District Court) within two months of the refusal decision; and (iii) simultaneously file a fresh clearance request with a modified distinguishing element to avoid delay in the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for incorporation where a licensed domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999 provides the registered office. However, the SARL must maintain adequate economic substance in Luxembourg — including effective local management, employees or contracted personnel, accounting records kept in Luxembourg, a Luxembourg bank account, and board decision-making functions conducted locally. For a digital webnovel subscription platform monetized through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, a purely virtual registered address is legally possible, but tax-residency robustness requires demonstrable local substance; the risk of challenge by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) increases if the company functions only as a mailbox entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS, CSSF, or tax authorities is estimated at 5–10% for a standard low-risk, compliant SARL; the likelihood rises to 15–25% where the company relies exclusively on a domiciliation address without demonstrable operating substance or where Apple/Google revenue flows are not matched by local operating expenditure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 442-1 et seq. (SARL) and the general provisions of the law applicable to companies with share capital
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation) followed by publication in RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum EUR 12,000; capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Luxembourg bank account or placed in notarial escrow, evidenced by a blocked funds certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOR THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND PARTNERS OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L.: Upon the notarial execution of the articles of incorporation, the initial shareholder(s) and the appointed chairman of the constitutive general meeting hereby RESOLVE: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The statutory share capital of EUR 15,000 is fully subscribed and paid up in cash as evidenced by bank certificate, and each subscriber's rights are accepted. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg; the gérant is empowered to negotiate and sign the lease. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENT: [NAME], residing at [ADDRESS], is appointed as gérant, with sole authority to operate the company's bank accounts and represent the company until removal. 4. DELEGATION: The notary and the gérant are authorized to complete all RCS filings and registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and RCS availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability request via the online RCS platform for the intended corporate name. The RCS issues a non-confusion certificate and reserves the name for two months. The name must include the suffix 's.à r.l.' or 'SARL'.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Identification particulars of each proposed partner
Proof of intended registered office (optional at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to prior reservation or confusion, submit an alternative distinctive name through the same portal; no substantive legal obstacle, only a new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signature of the notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the articles of association and execute the incorporation deed before all partners. The deed must state subscriptions, contributions, registered office, corporate purpose, and management rules of the SARL.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft articles of association prepared by counsel
Valid passport or national ID of each partner and manager
Lease proposal or letter of intent for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, amend the draft and schedule a new signature date; any inaccurate contribution statement must be rectified before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum share capital in bank or notarial escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or qualified notarial escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transfer the subscribed cash capital to an escrow account in the name of the company in formation or to the notary's client account. Obtain a blocking certificate (certificat de blocage) confirming the amount and that it cannot be withdrawn until RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account proof / blocked account statement
AML source-of-funds information for each subscriber
Wire transfer receipt or deposit confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays, use another eligible Luxembourg credit institution or obtain from the notary an equivalent blocking confirmation; capital remains frozen pending incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RCS filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the notary submits the deed and attachments to the RCS for registration of legal existence, registered office, and appointment of the gérant. The RCS verifies formalities and issues a registration extract.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Bank blocking certificate
Power of attorney if the notary submits electronically
Proof of registered office lease or authorization
Identification particulars of the appointed gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, provide supplementary documents or amend the deed within 15 working days via the same electronic filing channel; the application may be re-submitted with corrected information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of incorporation notice in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS publishes the statutory incorporation notice in RESA concurrently with or immediately after registration. The publication ensures legal opposability to third parties; retain the RESA extract as evidence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Confirmation of registered office and corporate purpose
Payment receipt for publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice is delayed or defective, contact RCS e-Support to request a corrected or supplemental publication; registration validity remains effective from the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ADMINISTRATION DES CONTRIBUTIONS DIRECTES (ACD); ADMINISTRATION DE L'ENREGISTREMENT, DES DOMAINES ET DE LA TVA (AEDT); CENTRE COMMUN DE LA SÉCURITÉ SOCIALE (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS extract, file for corporate income tax, VAT identification, and employer registration through the MyGuichet.lu portal. Enrol the company and the gérant with CCSS if remuneration is paid.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarial deed and articles of association
Identity details of managers
Bank account IBAN of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late eligibility is cured by submission through MyGuichet.lu with a brief explanatory note; tax and VAT registrations may be made effective retroactively to the RCS incorporation date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — pure-digital web-novel subscription platform with no physical manufacturing or industrial establishment; no industrial licence required under Luxembourg law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; if payment processing or hosting becomes regulated, separate financial or telecom licensing conditions may apply, but the core content activity remains license-exempt

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure administrative/office activity; no EIA required under Luxembourg Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOCs, or dust emissions. Office operations must comply with municipal wastewater standards, EU WEEE directive for e-waste, and local waste sorting obligations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: compliance with Grand-Ducal Regulation on fire protection in office buildings, including exit routes, extinguishers, and signage. Occupational clearance: risk assessment filed with and inspected by the ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines), and workers' health and safety registration with the occupational health service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for corporate income tax; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT; electronic filing through MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SARL must first be incorporated and registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS); the ACD then issues the corporate Luxembourg tax identification number (TIN). For VAT, a separate application for a VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) must be submitted to the AEDT via MyGuichet, attaching the deed of incorporation, RCS extract, director identification, and a description of intended activities. A non-resident entity with no Luxembourg fixed establishment making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly for Luxembourg VAT before its first taxable transaction and, when required by the AEDT, appoint an approved fiscal representative. Registration triggers periodic VAT return obligations (monthly or quarterly).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Luxembourg SARL is a resident full taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IF) on worldwide profits; no pass-through classification is available for a SARL; no tax-exempt zone applies to digital publishing or subscription platform activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; classification follows statutory legal form (SARL is treated as a corporation). Available elections include: (i) fiscal unity / group taxation for CIT under Article 164bis LIR (95% ownership chain, 5-year irrevocable commitment); (ii) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) applicable since 1 January 2023; (iii) IP box election granting an 80% exemption for qualifying IP income subject to nexus requirements; (iv) R&D super-deduction election for eligible software and content-development expenditure; and (v) the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) election for declaring EU cross-border B2C digital subscription sales centrally in Luxembourg.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) under the Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business exemption: EUR 35,000 annual turnover; non-resident suppliers of digital services: no registration threshold (registration mandatory from the first euro of taxable supplies in Luxembourg); EU-wide cross-border B2C distance-sale threshold for optional supplier-country taxation: EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API, or digital stamping regime applies in Luxembourg. Mandatory structured e-invoicing applies only to business-to-government (B2G) supplies via the PEPPOL network (EN 16931). Draft law (Bill 8277) proposes phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing for Luxembourg-established suppliers, with expected commencement in 2025 for entities above EUR 100,000 turnover and in 2026 for all entities, although final enactment remains pending. VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and OSS filings are submitted electronically via MyGuichet; taxpayers must retain standardized electronic accounting files (eCDF / SAF-T-compatible) for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported to non-EU destinations qualify for zero-rating under Article 41 of the Luxembourg VAT law, provided the export is evidenced to the AEDT. For the webnovel subscription platform: B2C digital services supplied to non-EU consumers fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope because the place of supply is the consumer's country of usual residence; B2B supplies of digital content licensing to non-EU taxable persons are outside Luxembourg VAT scope (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction); B2C supplies to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's country, and the SARL may declare such sales centrally under the Union OSS scheme; where the SARL's intra-EU cross-border B2C turnover does not exceed EUR 10,000, Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies instead.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration under the EU Union Customs Code (UCC) with export clearance evidence (Export Control System / AES) for any physical goods exported
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or CMR transport document proving physical departure from EU customs territory (for any transiting goods or promotional merchandise)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT statements or acquirer settlement reports evidencing receipt of consideration from the foreign customer
Digital service audit trail: consumer geo-location, IP address, billing and cardholder address, App Store / Google Play transaction receipts, and subscription log records
Signed subscription terms, platform revenue records, and retained VAT OSS registration validity documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT audits cross-border zero-rating and OSS positions closely. Unsupported export zero-rating or erroneous non-application of Luxembourg VAT results in retrospective VAT assessment at 17% plus late-payment interest, penalty fines (amendes), and, in serious cases, additional surcharges of up to 10% of the tax due. VAT fraud is criminally sanctionable, with extension of the statutory assessment window from 5 to 10 years, clawback of previously refunded VAT, joint and several liability of directors, and potential imprisonment under the Luxembourg General Tax Code and Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg) within the Eurosystem, with the European Central Bank (ECB) as the supranational monetary authority; capital-movement and foreign-exchange policy is governed at EU level under TFEU Articles 63–66, and Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange-control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full, unrestricted convertibility for both current and capital account transactions as a founding Eurozone member and an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction; the euro is legal tender and corporate balances may be freely held in EUR or any convertible currency. No prior exchange-control approval or license is required for payments or remittances. Profit-remittance hurdles arise principally from withholding tax rather than FX controls: dividends distributed by a SARL are subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at the domestic 15% rate unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the domestic Luxembourg participation exemption (minimum 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition value, with a 12-month minimum holding period); no withholding tax applies to royalties or ordinary interest payments to EU/EEA corporate recipients under domestic law. Routine cross-border remittances require only standard bank-level FX documentation and, where requested, balance-of-payments statistical declarations to the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, surrender obligation, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. A Luxembourg SARL exporting digital-content subscription services (including net settlements received from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts indefinitely in any currency at any authorised credit institution, with no statutory deadline or minimum-EUR conversion requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Blocked Account (compte bloqué) for SARL incorporation plus EUR Operational Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with Cash Management and T2 settlement
Operational Account plus Trade Finance and Commercial Letter of Credit Account
Cooperative SME Operational Account (EUR clearing and sweep)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for Luxembourg/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions operating under the PSD2 passport (e.g., Adyen Luxembourg, Stripe Payments Europe, Payoneer EU entity), which are suitable treasury rails for multi-currency payouts and platform mass disbursements. Rating: Low for offshore/non-EEA EMIs (UK FCA-regulated e-money issuers, US state-licensed money transmitters, Singapore or Hong Kong e-money providers), which cannot participate in Eurosystem T2 clearing or offer SEPA-instant EUR settlement without an EEA license. Legal constraints: under the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and e-money and CSSF Regulation 10-02, the SARL may hold funds in an EMI account, but funds held outside a licensed credit institution are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDL up to EUR 100,000); the EMI must demonstrate safeguarding of client funds, and the SARL remains subject to CSSF Circular 12-02 AML/CFT obligations when appointing an EMI as payout agent for author royalties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML legislation (Law of 19 December 2002, CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended) does not statutorily mandate physical presence; banks must identify directors and ultimate beneficial owners using reliable, independent-source documentation. In practice: (i) EU/EEA-resident directors can complete fully remote onboarding through eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signatures or recognised EU e-ID schemes; (ii) non-EU directors, or directors acting under powers of attorney, are typically required to attend a physical meeting at the bank's Luxembourg office or, where bank policy permits, a live videoconference with notarised or apostilled identity documents; (iii) banks will request the RBE extract from the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners, the notarised articles of association, and a named local AML-file custodian before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect ownership-chain opacity where the UBO of the Luxembourg SARL cannot be clearly determined through layered intermediate holding companies or trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of association and share register; RBE extract; full organisational chart; corporate resolutions and incorporation certificates of each intermediate holding tier; sworn source-of-wealth statement for each UBO; and certified passport copies for all shareholders holding more than 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border consumer digital receipts via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing without visible underlying content performance or merchant attribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program and Google Play consignment and settlement agreements including merchant identifiers; periodic settlement reports showing net revenue, currency conversion and fee deductions; content-rights and author-royalty contracts; ISIC 9000 web-novel catalogue licences; and a process map demonstrating that retail payments never touch the SARL's own bank accounts directly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU directors or UBOs resident in a FATF high-risk or EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdiction triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or certified passports and recent residential certificates; tax-residence certificates; bank references; notarised declaration of source of funds and source of wealth; PEP and sanctions screening results (EU consolidated list, UN lists, OFAC SDN); and a documented commercial rationale for board composition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared 'Low_Risk_Standard' AML tier and the projected recurring subscription payment volumes, triggering a bank-side risk-rating override.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML risk-assessment file justifying the low-risk classification (no cash, no crypto-asset flows, no embargoed-market sales, transparent UBO identification, established payment intermediaries); documented transaction-monitoring methodology with thresholds; subscription-terms and refund-policy documentation; and confirmation from the Luxembourg AML compliance officer accepting residual risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EUR capital injections should be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer (or SEPA Instant where available) from the investor's bank directly to the SARL's blocked capital account, or via SWIFT MT103 where the shareholder is outside SEPA. Recommended EBA/ISO 20022 purpose code: INTC (intra-company payment) for shareholder loans and intercompany advances; LOAN for formal intercompany debt; for equity contributions, banking practice requires supporting evidence rather than reliance on a purpose code — the notarised capital-increase deed, updated RBE filing, shareholders' resolution, and the notary's capital-release certificate. Verification steps: T2 settlement confirmation, SWIFT MT103/MT202 acknowledgment, sanctions and AML screening clearance (EU consolidated list, UN, OFAC), and BCL balance-of-payments statistical forms where requested by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR trade settlements (author royalties, content-licensing fees, external marketing payments) and SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant for EUR payables; documentary Letters of Credit (URC 522 / ISP98) and demand guarantees for high-value content-rights acquisitions; correspondent banking via the BCL/T2 Luxembourg (LuxCSD) for EUR clearing and via US and UK correspondents for USD and GBP clearing. For recurring low-value author royalties, a Luxembourg-licensed payment institution with mass-payout APIs is permitted, with full audit-trail reporting to the SARL's core banking relationship.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) up to 12 months from Luxembourg-licensed credit institutions
FX swaps and swap-points transactions via authorised bank counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible or restricted-account EMEA/APAC currencies (e.g., CNY, KRW, IDR, TRY) through internationally authorised offshore desks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for synthetic EUR/USD or EUR/GBP treasury funding
Plain-vanilla European-option FX options for subscription-revenue hedging, subject to MiFID II appropriateness and CSSF conduct rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial summons; fine up to EUR 1,500 per director; potential administrative strike-off from RCS after repeated notices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation (Confirmation des ayants droit économiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 September, or within one month after the AGM approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deliberate non-filing: fine up to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months; temporary lapses subject to remedial notices and administrative fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SARL only when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average workforce > 50. Shareholders holding at least 10% of equity may request an audit even below thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalisé), aligned with EU Directive 2013/34; IFRS compulsory only for listed undertakings or consolidated accounts of certain public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an internal UBO register at the registered office and file all UBO data with the RCS. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days. Annually, after approval of the annual accounts, the SARL must confirm via RCS that the published UBO information remains accurate and complete.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (or Register of Director Decisions, if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,200 - 3,500 (typical annual fee for Luxembourg registered office and corporate agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000 - 20,000 (typical certified audit for a small to medium SARL if audit becomes compulsory or is requested)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City for taxable profits above EUR 175,000 (17% CIT + 7% unemployment fund surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); reduced aggregate of 22.80% for the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% deduction for qualifying intellectual property income, yielding an approximate 4.99% effective aggregate rate; investment tax credit of 7% on qualifying investments (capped at EUR 50,000); participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gains income
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (unlimited carryforward; no statutory time limit, subject to anti-abuse on change of business activity; no carryback)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 830 (corporate income tax return, 'Déclaration pour l'impôt sur les sociétés') filed with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) via MyGuichet.lu / e-Tax online portal; municipal business tax is combined in Model 830-A where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (quarterly prepayments of estimated CIT are required during the accounting period)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Model 830 return must be filed by 31 July following the close of the financial year; the ACD routinely grants extensions of up to 6 months on a justified request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: company name, RCS number, registered office address, legal form (SARL), and tax identification number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE address and its Luxembourg tax representative; a non-resident with no PE is not required to file this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements: balance sheet and profit and loss account for the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Luxembourg PE accounts or a clearly allocated foreign-currency financial statement converted into EUR with notes on transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computation: net accounting profit after fiscal adjustments, depreciation, provisions, and disallowed expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the PE taxable profit using the OECD authorized OECD approach and applicable Luxembourg DTA rules; do not include worldwide profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward: amount of previously recognized Luxembourg corporate tax losses utilized to reduce current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses attributable to the Luxembourg PE may be deducted; evidence of business continuity and change-of-ownership restrictions must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemptions and deductions: participation exemption, IP Box deduction, notional interest deduction, and foreign tax credit calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders claiming treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive protection must provide a valid tax residence certificate and demonstrate entitlement to reducing withholding taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and payments: prepayments made, withholding tax credits, and the net wealth tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare Luxembourg withholding tax recovered or recoverable on Luxembourg-source income, and attach the relevant tax vouchers and refund application forms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a default assessment and penalty of 10% to 20% of the tax due depending on the tax authorities' discretion; late payment interest accrues at 10% per annum, and intentional omission or fraudulent filing exposes the company to criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; 0% where the Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies to a qualifying EU corporate shareholder; treaty reductions typically lower the rate to 0–5%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payer must obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority plus a formal claim for reduction on the appropriate ACD form (usually Form 25.22 or e-Tax submission through MyGuichet). For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the shareholder must prove a 10% capital shareholding held for at least 12 months and complete a summary declaration. Luxembourg applies treaty withholding relief at source where formalities are completed before the payment; otherwise refund can be claimed from the ACD within the statutory period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding tax on arm's length royalties and interest paid to non-resident companies is 0%; profit-participating loans may be treated as equity and subject to 15% withholding, but most Luxembourg DTAs reduce the rate to 0–10%. Royalties for copyrighted webnovel content used in Luxembourg are generally free from withholding for the non-resident beneficial owner absent a Luxembourg PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File are required under Luxembourg law (EU TPD implementation) when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750 million; below this threshold the ACD may request contemporaneous documentation for material cross-border related-party transactions, generally where such transactions exceed EUR 500,000 annually in aggregate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the offshore style, but permanent residence and treaty benefits depend on substantive local presence: place of effective management in Luxembourg, local board decisions, operational staff, premises, and DEMPE for IP holding. The ACD applies general anti-abuse rules and EU ATAD principles; a SARL functioning as a pure mail-box owner of a webnovel platform will be denied Luxembourg residence and treaty shelter.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Fraud and Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting digital subscription and in-app purchase revenue (Apple IAP / Google Play) from the Luxembourg corporate income tax return, inflating deductible costs with fictitious royalty or advertising charges, or maintaining double set of books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg criminal tax law, deliberate filing of false returns is punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, plus fraudulent assessment surcharges of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax and 10% per annum late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in filing false returns or drowning the SARL in debt are subject to individual criminal liability, joint and several payment of the evaded tax if the company becomes insolvent, and procedures may include travel bans and confiscation of assets under the Luxembourg Code of Criminal Procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SARL exclusively as a conduit to hold webnovel platform contracts and IP rights while all editorial, technical, marketing, procurement, and decision-making functions occur outside Luxembourg with minimal local staff and no real economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities may disregard the Luxembourg entity as a sham, reassess profits at the foreign de facto parent level, impose 100% bad-faith penalties, deny DTA benefits and EU Directives, and apply the ATAD / GAAR anti-abuse provisions, resulting in retroactive taxation at a punitive rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell SARL can be held civilly liable for the company's tax liabilities under the doctrine of déclaration frauduleuse, may be subjected to personal corporate bans, travel restrictions, and criminal penalties for facilitating tax evasion if the shell is used to hide beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, management fees, or interest streams to a Hong Kong, US, or other low-tax affiliate with no DEMPE evidence for the webnovel catalogue, leaving artificially thin margins in Luxembourg and eroding the local tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Luxembourg tax law (Art. 56 LIR) with reallocation of profits to Luxembourg, late-payment interest of 10% per annum, and penalties ranging from 10% to 50% of the additional tax assessed; failure to maintain an adequate TP file may itself attract a separate documentation fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Consultant-level fault (faute lourde) of directors in approving non-arm's length arrangements can make directors personally liable to the tax authorities for the related tax insufficiencies, and criminal sanctions apply if the transfer pricing scheme is used to commit money laundering or intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file and update the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) for the SARL, concealing the ultimate controlling shareholder of the webnovel serial platform, or processing high-volume consumer payments from app stores while lacking adequate AML/KYC procedures for related capital movements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg laws on the RBE register and AML/CFT, failure to register or to keep accurate beneficial ownership information is a criminal offense punishable by fines of up to EUR 25,000 per violation; AML supervision fines for commercial entities can escalate to EUR 2 million or 10% of annual turnover, and the register may publish sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors and statutory managers are personally criminally liable for deliberate non-disclosure of the beneficial owner, with imprisonment up to 3 years; they may also be prohibited from exercising management functions and be subjected to travel bans during any money laundering investigation where platform payment flows are considered criminal proceeds.
